questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they had English courses available. That they had a good student environment and other international students to connect with. That they had good and interesting courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Corona made it a little difficult, especially for the social aspect. Not as many events as before, but other than this a great experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was easy. However, I would have liked it if I was given more information about different social events they had for Erasmus students. Such as which Facebook groups to be part of and so on

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an online meeting that gave us different kinds of information. However, since it was online we experience some technical difficulties.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just filled out a form that was pretty easy and then I got a student dorm assigned. It wasn't on campus but it was not that far away from it and it was pretty cheap

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That as long as you are living close to the city or public transportation it doesn't matter whether or nt you are living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was nice having my own room and having a girl as a roommate to share the bathroom and the kitchen with. It was located right next to public transportation which was nice, however, the social life at the student dorm was not really there due to corona. Also, it would have been nice to maybe share a room with another international student or to live together with other international students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did not register for classes. My Erasmus coordinator from Heidelberg registered for me. I just told her which courses I wanted to attend and then she wrote back to me about whether or not it was possible. My Erasmus coordinator from Heidelberg was very very helpful and if I had any questions I could just ask her.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Well, we had an intro week where some tutors would give you all sorts of information including how to register. If you had problems they would also help you

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most of the courses were a succes, however, I did have to find one new course since the class wouldn't be in English as thought.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That it can be quite complicated but that you shouldn't stress about it. Just sign up for the introduction week and they will help you. I would also strongly recommend to find you Erasmus coordinator from your department since they can help you with everything including registering for courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the system was just not for me. Also, I did experience some problems with English communication. Furthermore, it seemed in general that the workload did not at all match the credits that were given for the geoinformatics courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was quite high. In my courses a lot of master's degrees students attended. Also since some of my courses required some background knowledge about the landscape in the region I lacked that knowledge. I also took a lot of geoinformatics courses without knowing that the workload for these type of courses is quite high and therefore I struggled more.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. Didn't have exams but was grated from the assignments we handed in during the semester. I did not have that many lectures but a lot of assignments that we needed to hand in all the time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: GIS Analyses using Free and Open Source Software, OSM land use, Geländepraktikum: Bodengeographie/Geomorphologie,  Geländepraktikum in Hydrologie und Klimatologie, Untersuchung von Klimawandel und Klimawandelfolgen mithilfe von Methoden der räumlichen Statistik und Zeitreihenanalyse, General language course, Basic 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The field trip (Geländepraktikum in Hydrologie und Klimatologie) was a very nice experience. So beautiful. Would recommend it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had one. Buying a semester ticket is a good way to save money on public transportation. It costs around 1300 dkk and is valid for all public transportation in Heidelberg and also in some other cities for the entire semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, it was cheaper to live in Heidelberg than in Copenhagen. Housing was cheaper. food was cheaper. Phone companies a little bit more expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think they did what they could with corona still being there. I think way more events would have been possible otherwise

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know you could join volleyball and I think football as well. I don't really remember what else

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any athletic activities, but if you are part of some groups on Whatsapp they will tell you about an event on a bar every week and also about certain trips to other cities you can sign up for

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See Munich, go to the alps and hike. See Stuttgart, Frankfurt. and also Schwetzingen (is really beautiful in the spring when the cherry trees blossom). In general just see Heidelberg, the castle, the railway and the Philosophenweg. The zoo does also have an event in the autumn/ winter called zoo light that s very cool

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is pretty easy. However, the language barrier is noticeable when going to certain store and shops

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for a buddy. You will probably receive an email where you can sign up for a buddy who will help you with different kinds of stuff and also just to socialize with. It is a really good idea. This way you meet a local person who then can help you meet others.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Important to have cash. Not every store accepts credit cards. Also, it is a little old-fashioned with how you should speak and write to your professors. It is more formal, and you never address them by their first name

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Can't really explain. Everything was just really cool. people are so sweet and the food was really good as well

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the workload, that geoinformatics courses have a high workload, so I would recommend max choosing two per semester. 

???

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just that the city is so beautiful. I loved going for walks and just go through the center and the very long shopping street. Going to the castle and seeing the amazing view. There are so many young and international people, they are all so sweet and you easily feel at home and that you belong

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses were very challenging and speaking English instead of German could sometimes also creates some difficulties and miscommunications

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
